analysis:
Both units are head-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md, a documentation-only file (lines 544-1007, historical release notes v0.9.18 through the tail of the v0.10.1 candidate section). The patch shows only prose changes, a new v0.10.1 candidate header and upgrade notes, and no executable code, configuration, workflow or key-handling changes are visible in the supplied evidence. No finding qualifies.

Security-relevant claims described in the text that integration should treat as unverified documentation, not as evidence of implemented controls:
- The staging environment and its relaxed installer signature check for `-dev.`/`-staging.` versions (lines 633-647). Production is kept on the full Apple-team requirement, and prod releases are tag-gated. The underlying `scripts/install.sh` and workflow changes are in other files that were not supplied. Whether the relaxation is correctly limited to pre-release versions (relevant to T-013, T-034, TB-009 and A-011) needs review of those files.
- The SSD checkpoint staging cap raised to 7 GiB / 15 s on large Macs (lines 588-597), the segment retention (lines 549-550) and the cache storage controls (lines 800-802) relate to T-041. The notes claim the daily write cap and encryption are unchanged. The source code was not supplied, so TTL, HMAC naming, AAD and salt scoping cannot be validated.
- The rollout note (head diff) says logprobs are refused by the platform coordinator before reservation and that old providers fail with a 500 that cools every provider of the model. That is a coordinator-side availability dependency, not a provider regression visible here.
- The automatic official provider release registration (line 851) removes manual per-release qualification. This is a documented policy and relates to A-011/A-017 and T-054. It is not a change in this diff, which only restates it.

No uncertainty in the supplied changelog text affects a security conclusion. The remaining integration questions are about the code in other files for the staging installer relaxation and the SSD cache changes.
